merger_description:
Parker-Hannifin Corporation (**Parker-Hannifin**) proposes to acquire the Aerospace and Defense business of CIRCOR International, Inc. (**CIRCOR A&D**).

Parker-Hannifin is a global engineering company headquartered in the United States. It designs, manufactures and supplies motion and control technologies and systems, and provides engineered solutions for a variety of mobile, industrial and aerospace applications.

CIRCOR A&D designs, manufactures and supports flight-critical motion and flow control products for commercial aircraft and defence applications with manufacturing and operational locations in the United States, France and Morocco.

Parker-Hannifin and CIRCOR A&D both supply fluid control valves for industrial applications in Australia.

events.title: Parker-Hannifin–CIRCOR A&D - Phase 1 determination
events.determination_commission_division: Determination made by Commissioner Williams pursuant to a delegation under section 25(1) of the Act

determination_table_content.details:
Parker-Hannifin Corporation (Parker-Hannifin)’s proposed
acquisition of the Aerospace and Defense business of CIRCOR
International, Inc. (CIRCOR A&D).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABZE(1) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition may be put into effect.

The acquirer, Parker-Hannifin, is a global engineering company
headquartered in the United States. It designs, manufactures and
supplies motion and control technologies and systems, and provides
engineered solutions for a variety of mobile, industrial and
aerospace applications.
The target, CIRCOR A&D, designs, manufactures and supports flight-
critical motion and flow control products for commercial aircraft and
defence applications with manufacturing and operational locations
in the United States, France and Morocco. To a more limited extent,
CIRCOR A&D also supplies products for industrial applications.

Globally, Parker-Hannifin and CIRCOR A&D (the Parties) are both
active in the supply of certain aerospace valves and switches.
Parker-Hannifin primarily supplies system-level packages of
products that include component parts (including valves and
switches), while CIRCOR A&D supplies individual component parts.
In Australia, the Parties both supply fluid control valves for industrial
applications. CIRCOR A&D does not supply aerospace products in
Australia.

When making a determination in Phase 1, the Australian Competition
and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition
assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an
acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in
Phase 2 in accordance with section 51ABZJ of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act). In doing so, the ACCC must have
regard to the object of the Act and all relevant matters, including the
interests of consumers.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notified acquisitions, see the ACCC’s merger assessment guidelines
and interim merger process guidelines.
In conducting its competition assessment, the ACCC has considered
the information and documents that were submitted with the
notification form and information from third parties.
The ACCC has determined that the Acquisition may be put into
effect as it considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to have the
effect of substantially lessening competition in any market. In
reaching its decision, and based on the material before it, the ACCC
makes the following findings.
• The market aggregation resulting from the Acquisition in the
supply of fluid control valves for industrial applications in
Australia is estimated to be low.
• There is no horizontal overlap between the Parties in the supply
of aerospace components in Australia.
• The Parties would likely continue to be constrained by
alternative global suppliers of aerospace valves and switches.

A notifying party, or other person who has been allowed to do so by
the Australian Competition Tribunal, may apply for review if they are
dissatisfied with the determination. Pursuant to section 100C of the
Act, applications for review of the determination are to be made to
the Australian Competition Tribunal before the end of 14 calendar
days after this statement of reasons was included on the ACCC’s
Acquisitions Register. To confirm whether there has been any
application for review, please contact the Australian Competition
Tribunal.
